summary: QuBE/Qubex is an integrated hardware-software control system combining broadband microwave generation (1.6 GHz instantaneous span, 7.25–10 GHz control, 9.5–11 GHz readout, 19–21 GHz pump) with a pulse-level software framework for scalable superconducting qubit experiments. Validation on a 64-qubit fixed-frequency transmon chip demonstrates automated setup, synchronized multi-unit operation, far-detuned cross-resonance gates with 98.34 % fidelity, and multilevel readout achieving 95.4 % state-assignment fidelity with JPA assistance.
motivation: Large-scale fixed-frequency transmon systems operating in the far-detuned regime require broadband, high-power, phase-coherent control across distributed hardware units, coupled with software that reliably translates chip metadata and calibration state into reproducible experimental configurations and pulse sequences.
method: QuBE provides multi-unit clock distribution (100 MHz, 250 MHz, 62.5 kHz references), FPGA-based arbitrary waveform generation with three-channel frequency synthesis per control port, and synchronized readout with parametric-amplifier pump support; Qubex resolves qubit frequencies, wiring, and hardware parameters into LO/CNCO/FNCO/AWG terms and implements automated spectroscopy, coherence characterization, and two-qubit calibration workflows.
result: On the 64-qubit platform: single-qubit $X_{\pi/2}$ gate fidelity of 99.963 ± 0.003 %, far-detuned CR gate (Q28–Q25, $\Delta_{ct} = -729.3$ MHz) fidelity of 98.34 ± 0.08 %, and multilevel readout of $|g\rangle$, $|e\rangle$, $|f\rangle$ with 99.5 %, 95.7 %, and 91.2 % assignment probabilities respectively with JPA amplification. Phase stability across 3600 s measured below 0.456°; neighboring-port crosstalk suppression 88.0 dB; third-order IMD suppression 56.4 dB.
